title: The American Diabetes Association and Vera Health Collaborate to Expand Access to the Standards of Care in Diabetes
summary: Clinicians using Vera can now consult the American Diabetes Association’s Standards of Care in Diabetes and professional resources in seconds, cited and linked to the original source.
body_markdown:
**Clinicians using Vera can now consult the American Diabetes Association’s *Standards of Care in Diabetes* and professional resources in seconds, cited and linked to the original source.**


San Francisco and Arlington, Va., November 18, 2026. Vera Health announced a collaboration with the American Diabetes Association® (ADA) that brings the ADA’s *Standards of Care in Diabetes* (Standards of Care) to Vera. Vera is a medical search engine that finds, grades, and cites the best available evidence in seconds, used by more than 800,000 clinicians worldwide.


Diabetes is one of the fastest-moving fields in medicine. Every year, the ADA’s Professional Practice Committee for Diabetes updates the Standards of Care based on the latest scientific research and clinical trials. Through this collaboration, clinicians using Vera can ask a question and get an answer grounded in the ADA’s latest guidance.


“Clinical AI cannot be built in a vacuum,” said Taieb Bennani, co-founder of Vera Health. “Every year, the ADA convenes global experts to turn an enormous body of research into the standard that diabetes medicine in the United States and beyond is measured against. We’re honored to bring its guidance to clinicians wherever they practice.”


“Our collaborations start from a simple belief: the organizations that set the standard should be at the center of how clinicians reach it,” said Maxime Allouch, co-founder of Vera Health. “The ADA has led the field for more than eight decades, and in Vera, its guidance will always carry its name.”


Beyond the Standards of Care, the collaboration covers a selection of the ADA’s professional resources, including its clinical compendia, Healthcare Professional Resource Library, and selected professional publications. As guidance is updated, clinicians will see those same updates in Vera, allowing them to consult the latest and most current version.


“The American Diabetes Association is proud to provide the gold-standard in evidence-based guidelines for diagnosing and managing diabetes and prediabetes,” said Charles “Chuck” Henderson, the ADA’s chief executive officer. “But these standards are only helpful for people with diabetes if they are put into practice. By working with organizations like Vera, we aim to turn our standards of care into standards of practice to help people living with diabetes and prediabetes thrive.”


The collaboration is part of Vera’s work with the medical societies and professional organizations that shape medicine, including its[official partnership with the American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP)](https://www.verahealth.ai/blog/acep-vera-health-partner-trusted-ai-emergency-physicians) .


## About Vera Health


Vera Health is a medical search engine built to reason like a clinician. It finds the evidence first, grades it with a framework built alongside the physicians who write practice guidelines, and shows the source, strength and limits behind every answer, in seconds. Designed exclusively for healthcare professionals, Vera is used by more than 800,000 clinicians, including more than one in four doctors in countries like Spain and Italy, and has been the world’s most downloaded app for clinicians every month since June 2026. Vera is free for licensed clinicians and trainees and never trains on clinicians’ questions. It is HIPAA and GDPR compliant, SOC 2 Type II certified and aligned with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. Founded in 2024 at Y Combinator by Taieb Bennani and Maxime Allouch, Vera Health has raised $32 million from investors including Threshold Ventures, Gradient, Y Combinator, SV Angel and Mantis VC, and is headquartered in San Francisco. Learn more at[verahealth.ai](https://www.verahealth.ai/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=ada_collaboration&utm_content=cta) .
